name: East International
summary: The test field's crossing airliner airport, Cape International's layout laid on its own 09/27 and 18/36: the same taxiways, exits, gates, terminal and tower, the same FAA AC 150/5300-13B standards for the 747-400.
frame: Metres, in the frame of runway 09/27 (airfield testfield_east_09_27): `along` from its middle toward its far end, which is the WEST end and 09's threshold (a 90-degree runway's threshold is its east end); `across` from its centreline, positive to the NORTH. Runway 18/36 (airfield testfield_east_18_36) runs across the frame at along -700; its places are named `testfield_east_18_36.threshold` (the south end, 36's threshold, across -2,850), `testfield_east_18_36.far_end`, `testfield_east_18_36.centreline` and `testfield_east_18_36.edge`, which is its centreline plus half its width -- on its WEST side here, the apron's side. Otherwise as the fighter base's file.

sources.document: FAA Advisory Circular 150/5300-13B, Airport Design, change 1 with errata (public domain): https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC-150-5300-13B-Airport-Design-Chg1-w-errata.pdf. The design craft is the 747-400: airplane design group V, taxiway design group 5, approach category D; runways with approach visibility below 3/4 mile. Every figure below is from it unless it says otherwise.
sources.apron_craft: The 747-400 (Sim.Kind.JUMBO, 64.9 m span): the widest craft the taxilane and the remote stands are laid for. The 737 gates name their own craft, the 737-800 (ADG III). The plan spaces each apron's stands a span plus wingtip_to_wingtip apart.
sources.runway_to_taxiway: Table G-11 (C/D/E-V): runway centreline to parallel taxiway centreline, 400 ft below 1,345 ft elevation. ICAO Annex 14 table 3-1 gives 172.5 m for code E; this layout keeps the FAA's.
sources.taxiway_obstacle_clearance: Table 4-1, ADG V: taxiway centreline to fixed or movable object, 142.5 ft.
sources.taxilane_obstacle_clearance: Table 4-1, ADG V: taxilane centreline to fixed or movable object, 135 ft. A nose-in gate's tail is kept this far off its taxilane's centreline.
sources.taxiway_to_taxilane: Table 4-1, ADG V: taxiway centreline to parallel taxiway centreline, 249.5 ft (the taxilane's own figure is less, 242 ft).
sources.hold_bar: Table G-11, footnote 8: runway centreline to holding position, 280 ft for a precision approach runway.
sources.wingtip_to_wingtip: Table 5-1: parking position clearance, 25 ft for ADG III to VI.
sources.wingtip_to_taxilane: Table 4-1, ADG V: wingtip clearance on a taxilane, 28 ft.
sources.exit_angle_degrees: Paragraph 4.8.5 and figure 4-19: an acute-angled (high-speed) exit meets the runway at 30 degrees.
sources.exit_radius: The same figure: the exit's radius of 1,500 ft. The plan lays the exit as its straight 30-degree line; the radius is cited for the view, not yet drawn.
sources.exit_places: Figure 4-18, read off the chart: half of category D aircraft reach an acute-angled exit by about 5,900 ft (1,800 m) from the threshold at sea level. Paragraph 4.8.4.2 allows exits in the middle third where no taxiway crosses. So one at 1,700 m on 09 and two on 36 at 1,700 and 2,250 m, all short of the runways' crossing (2,450 m from 09's threshold, 2,850 m from 36's), so a landing turns off before it.
sources.tower_height: Not a standard: the FAA's recent towers stand 121 ft (Asheville) and 141 ft (Northwest Arkansas) to the cab; this one is 37 m to the cab's roof. From search summaries, not the pages themselves.
sources.tower_cab: Not a standard: a cab 9 m square, about a small tower's.
sources.terminals: Not a standard: a two-storey terminal, 15 m high. Its face stands 7 m past the gates' nose line.
sources.fillet: Not a published figure: the pavement added round a junction, wider than the fighter base's 15 m for a 747's wheelbase.
sources.layout: Copied from world/airbases/cape_international (lane/airport, 2026-09-19) with its runways renamed: the test field's 09/27 lies where the cape's does relative to its 18/36 (world/airfields/testfield_east_09_27), so every along and across here means the same place.
